cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its research objectives and hypotheses. (1) Research hypotheses or questions are provided: The authors explicitly state two hypotheses: that individuals with CNVs related to cognitive deficits will have larger deviation scores compared to a reference model, and that patterns of deviation across brain regions will be highly variable between CNV carriers. (2) The purpose of applying normative modeling is described: The authors describe using normative modeling to create personalized risk profiles, understand individual-level impacts of pathogenic CNVs on brain structure and behavior, and make cross-individual comparisons. Both criteria are satisfied.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "In this study, our primary objective is to dive into the individualized impacts of pathogenic CNVs on brain structure and behavior. By using a normative modeling approach, we take a step toward making personalized risk profiles that allow us to do cross-individual comparisons."; "We hypothesize that (1) individuals with a CNV related to cognitive deficits or neurodevelopmental disorders will have larger deviation scores compared with a reference model across several brain areas and (2) that the patterns of deviation across brain regions will be highly variable between these CNV carriers."
